messages:
Anya: Quick smoke report — ran a speculative-window-scan run on ozma-13b (8-bit) with k=2, prefetch_margin=12. Observed ~1.9x token/s vs non-spec baseline on our latency-sensitive workload, but saw intermittent degenerations on code tasks. Putting raw config + a tiny log below.

Sam: Nice. Can you paste the exact command + seed + metric script so we can reproduce? Also what was the fallback policy?

Anya: Yep — command I used: 
```
./run_infer.sh --model ozma-13b-8bit --spec-k 2 --prefetch 12 --fallback-prob 0.15 --batch 8 --seq 1024 --seed 42 
```
Eval was simple: 200 HumanEval-like prompts, pass@1 and token-level perplexity, plus our internal degen detector (repeated tokens / low entropy spans).

Lia: How are you defining "degeneration" for the detector? false positives on long comments can trigger it.

Anya: detector rule: >6 repeated token grams OR 30 tokens with entropy < 1.2 in a 64-token window. Manual spot-check: ~7 examples flagged, 5 are real regressions (duplicate lines), 2 are benign.

Sam: Can you share the quick numbers? throughput / ppl / pass@1 side-by-side?

Anya: short table (quick numbers):
- baseline (no spec): throughput 120 tok/s per GPU, ppl=12.10, pass@1=38.4%
- spec k=2, prefetch=12: throughput 230 tok/s per GPU, ppl=12.35, pass@1=37.7%
So ~1.9x speed, ~0.25 ppl delta, ~0.7% absolute drop on pass@1 for code. For chat/text prompts the drop is ~0.2% or within noise.

Lia: That's interesting — small quality hit concentrated on code. My guess: speculative proposals bias sampling toward higher-prob continuations that are syntactically valid but semantically wrong for code. Try lowering fallback_prob to 0.10 or increase speculative_k to 3? also run with deterministic sampling (top-p small) to understand whether sampling interacts.

Anya: will run variants. Planning a quick matrix tomorrow: fallback_prob in [0.05,0.10,0.15], speculative_k [1,2,3], seeds [42,99]. Also toggling prefix-KV cache warmup on/off.

Sam: Also add evaluation per task-type (doc, code, math). If code regresses more, consider a per-route policy: disable speculative on code endpoints or use a stricter fallback for them.

devbot: canary-run uploaded: s3://redwood-ci/spec-window/1768884321/results.tar.gz (contains raw logs, eval CSVs, rng seeds).

Anya: thanks — opening an internal issue with the main suspects and plan. TL;DR for ops: speculative-window-scan looks promising for throughput; needs tuned fallbacks for code workloads to avoid small but visible quality regressions.

Sam: SGTM. If you want I can slot a larger run later today (5k prompts) to reduce noise.

Anya: please do — also flag any reproducibility diffs (weird env flags we might've missed). cc @Lia

Lia: cool, I can also run a small targeted HumanEval subset with oracle filtering to see if regressions are semantic or just formatting.

Anya: will follow up with results in this thread. :thumbsup:
